markdown_report:
The strongest first experiment is a **jointly trained lexical residual inside the corrected HSTU**, selected using four-category macro validation HR@10. No improvement is claimed before evaluation.

**Insights and framework.** Three starting-point insights guide the proposal. (1) Users reject broad associations when precise function or content matters. Item-level identity alone may insufficiently share these distinctions. (2) Recent purchases can imply a completed need. Interaction histories cannot establish completion, so redundancy remains a hypothesis to test. (3) Electronics has 10.71% sampled wrong ranks and a −0.0749 lower-decile margin. Collapse scores near 0.5 provide little justification for collapse regularization.

Three literature insights suggest complementary directions. (1) [HSTU](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152) supports feature interactions within its sequential backbone. Additional representations can therefore remain part of one network. (2) [HLLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.12740) motivates jointly learning item text and sequence representations. Its architecture and gains do not establish benefits for this HSTU adaptation. (3) [AttrFormer](https://www.amazon.science/publications/learning-attribute-as-explicit-relation-for-sequential-recommendation) motivates explicit attribute distinctions. Title tokens provide imperfect evidence, not verified compatibility.

| Direction | Mechanism | Addressed gap |
|---|---|---|
| Objective | Multi-negative softmax | Confusing candidates |
| Temporal conditioning | Historical contribution gate | Stale demand |
| Representation | Gated lexical residual | Specific function/content |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. Each dimension includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

- **128-negative softmax:** 2/7/4/9/2. Originality: +HSTU precedent, −established; potential: +scalable discrimination, −false negatives; user: +finer ranking, −no explicit compatibility signal; model: +targets Electronics confusion, −sample margins may mislead; difficulty: +small change, −temperature tuning. Reference: [official HSTU configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin).
- **Recency gate:** 5/7/8/5/5. Originality: +content-conditioned timing, −existing temporal bias; potential: +adaptive relevance, −completion unobserved; user: +recent purpose, −repeat demand varies; model: +context discrimination, −weak direct diagnostic evidence; difficulty: +compact gate, −timestamp alignment. Reference: HSTU.
- **Lexical residual:** 4/8/8/7/4. Originality: +task-specific integration, −established text fusion; potential: +shared precise signals, −missing descriptions; user: +format/function distinctions, −compatibility uncertain; model: +disambiguates Electronics, −may amplify superficial similarity; difficulty: +small encoder, −tokenization and predictor consistency. References: HLLM, AttrFormer.

**Selected experiment.** At 0% progress, add only the lexical residual and retain the baseline objective and optimizer. Encode title/description tokens with randomly initialized embeddings; gate their pooled vector into each item representation inside the causal HSTU. Condition the gate on available history so content can support specific current intent.

This explicitly targets broad thematic recommendations and overlooked format/connector distinctions; Electronics separation is the quantitative target. Redundancy reduction is exploratory. Preserve one checkpoint/category, final nonpadding readout, diagnostic interfaces, seeds, routing, and training limits. Compare against the corrected baseline using the pinned macro validation metric; qualitative compatibility remains separately assessed.

idea.description: Add a small, jointly trained lexical residual to the supplied corrected HSTU. Encode public item titles and descriptions with randomly initialized token embeddings, and incorporate their pooled representations through learned gates within the existing network. Train exactly one model per category.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies overly broad associations and missed connector, format, dimension, and content distinctions. Lexical features may expose these distinctions to next-item learning. Electronics has the weakest measured sampled discrimination, with a 10.71% wrong-rank rate and a negative lower-decile margin; these measurements motivate testing more discriminative representations but do not establish held-out ranking performance.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve the supplied HSTU blocks, baseline loss, optimizer, sampler, and split logic for this first experiment. Build a deterministic vocabulary from public training-item titles/descriptions; preserve alphanumeric model identifiers and format markers. Cap token lengths and use a small masked-mean encoder initialized from scratch. Start residual gates near closed so initial behavior remains close to the baseline. Use a history-conditioned gate for sequence inputs and a shared item-side gate for candidate representations; these are jointly trained parts of the same network. Maintain item_emb as the actual ID embedding, log2feats(sequence) as the HSTU feature interface, and predict_score(features, items) as the canonical scorer that includes candidate lexical residuals. Diagnostics must call that scorer rather than reconstructing logits from item_emb alone. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), with measured metrics and definitions. Missing text yields a zero lexical residual. Read the final nonpadding position using the maximum valid index, never count minus one. Save vocabulary, item token buffers, architecture configuration, and weights beneath the trial directory; update the embedded predictor writer identically. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Retain all four dataset routes and load exactly one checkpoint per category. Use no reviews, unavailable attributes, pretrained weights, independent scoring models, or held-out labels for training. Select using fixed macro validation HR@10; report Electronics diagnostics separately without treating them as selection metrics.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    baseline = supplied_corrected_hstu(category)
    tokens = tokenize_public_titles_and_descriptions(training_item_catalog)
    model = HSTUWithLexicalResidual(baseline, tokens, random_initialization=True)

    # Within the same network:
    # text_i = masked_mean(token_embedding(tokens[i]))
    # candidate_i = id_embedding(i) + sigmoid(item_gate(id_embedding(i))) * project(text_i)
    # sequence_i = id_embedding(i) + sigmoid(history_gate(previous_state, text_i)) * project(text_i)
    # Previous-state conditioning must be causal and exclude the prediction target.

    for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
        for batch in range(200):
            sequence, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch()
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            positive_logits = model.predict_score(features, positive)
            negative_logits = model.predict_score(features, negative)
            loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(positive_logits, negative_logits, positive != 0)
            optimize(loss)
        evaluate_with_fixed_validation_protocol()
    save_single_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor_assets(model)

# In inference, gather max(position where sequence != 0), then call predict_score.
# Compare the completed four-category trial with baseline macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Combines precise lexical distinctions with the corrected HSTU through jointly trained residual gates under the single-model constraint.
originality.negative: Text fusion and residual gating are established techniques; novelty lies mainly in the constrained adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact route to sharing specific function and content evidence across sparse item histories.
future_potential.negative: Text may omit decisive compatibility information, and next-item supervision cannot verify fulfilled needs or actual product compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: A small pooling encoder and gates require limited architectural changes and no external models.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal history conditioning, candidate scoring, diagnostic adapters, and embedded predictor serialization must remain consistent.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU sequential transduction with feature gating and relative attention biases.
Provides the backbone that must be retained.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed lexical residual improves this Amazon benchmark.
Temporal and feature gates do not directly identify completed needs.

related_work.title: HLLM: Enhancing Sequential Recommendations via Hierarchical Large Language Models for Item and User Modeling
contributions: Motivates learning item-text and user-sequence representations through recommendation supervision.
Includes training from scratch as discussed in the supplied search evidence.
limitations: Pretrained initialization and reported gains cannot be assumed applicable under this task's constraints.

related_work.title: Learning Attribute-as-Explicit Relation for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Motivates modeling specific attribute relations beyond undifferentiated item similarity.
limitations: Lexical title and description tokens are incomplete proxies for attributes and compatibility.

related_work.title: Official HSTU sampled-softmax configuration
contributions: Supplies a practical precedent for 128 negatives, normalized embeddings, and temperature scaling.
limitations: Configuration choices are not established optima for these four Amazon datasets.
Supports a separate objective experiment rather than evidence for lexical residual gains.
